reports.title: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: Hims & Hers is providing the following guidance:

desk.headline: Revenue up 49% to $890m, slightly below estimates; 2026 EBITDA outlook cut, revenue range tightened
results: Revenue grew 49% to $890m, inside the company's $880-900m guide: US revenue rose 21% to $657m and international revenue more than quadrupled to $233m after acquisitions.
Gross margin fell to 57% from 74% as cheaper-margin branded weight-loss drugs and overseas sales grew in the mix.
The company swung to a net loss of $33.0m ($0.14 a share) from a $15.8m profit; adjusted EBITDA edged up to $82.4m but the margin fell to 9% from 13%.
Subscribers rose 13% to 2.79m, and revenue per subscriber jumped 30% to $105 a month.
Free cash flow dropped to $26.0m from $79.4m; cash was $606m plus $107m of short-term investments.

guidance.summary: Hims & Hers cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA range and tightened revenue to the lower half of its earlier range. Q4 revenue is guided to $875-895m, roughly flat on Q3.

points: Management deliberately held back US weight-loss marketing ahead of new drugs, pricing and longer subscription plans; subscribers fell by about 100,000 from Q2.
Zepbound and Foundayo are being added alongside Wegovy, with marketing set to ramp up around the Q1 seasonal peak.
The lower EBITDA outlook was tied to aggressive pricing and marketing in the UK and Germany and deferred weight-loss membership revenue.
A testosterone offering and a Peptides+ launch are planned for November, though peptides are not expected to move Q4 revenue much.
Management still targets positive free cash flow for 2026 and 2027.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks via Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov 2026; GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov 2026; prior ranges from the Q2 2026 results release

watch: Whether subscriber numbers recover once marketing restarts in Q1 2027.
Gross margin as branded GLP-1 drugs and international sales keep growing.
Early uptake of peptides and the wider weight-loss drug menu.
